data.name: Avishta
data.gender_notes: Avishta is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avishta is derived from the Sanskrit root 'vishta' meaning 'desire, aim, or wish'. It is believed that a child named Avishta will have strong desires and determination, and will strive to achieve their goals with dedication and hard work. The name Avishta carries the meaning “Desire, Aim, Wish” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Avishta usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, aim, wish and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Fulfilling one's deepest desires and aspirations.
data.etymology: Avishta belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, Aim, Wish.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avishta total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Avishta holds great significance in Hindu culture. It is often given to children who are expected to have a strong desire to excel in various fields of life. The name is believed to instill in the child a sense of determination, focus, and the willpower to overcome challenges.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Avishta is believed to signify the individual's innate desire for self-realization and the pursuit of truth. It is seen as a reminder of the deeper purpose of human existence, which is to awaken to the ultimate reality and live in accordance with it. The name is also believed to resonate with the divine principle of desire, which is a fundamental aspect of the human psyche, and can be harnessed for spiritual growth if channeled positively.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avishta: One who is steadfast and unwavering in their resolve, dedicated to their spiritual path and untouched by worldly desires.

historical_references.reference: Avishta was a powerful and influential sage, who is mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. He is known for his immense tapasya (penance) and was granted the boon of being immune to death by Lord Indra.
Avishta is also mentioned in the Puranic literature as a Rishi (sage) who cursed the moon god, Chandra, for neglecting his wife Rohini, resulting in Chandra's waning and waxing cycles.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Avishta, which originated from Hindu mythology, has gained modern relevance across various platforms and trends. In the field of astrobiology, researchers and scientists have shown interest in exploring the possibility of extra-terrestrial life forms, named as 'Avishtas', in the universe. Simultaneously, in the realm of AI and machine learning, Avishta is being used as a name for an advanced AI system or a neural network, symbolizing intelligence and wisdom. Lastly, in the context of wellness and spirituality, Avishta is used as a name for a meditation and mindfulness practice, derived from ancient Hindu traditions, to help individuals attain inner peace and wisdom.
